References and highlights: the places that name what the cursor is on,
in every file of the lib for a function, a variable, a macro, an object
or a header, in the document for a local or a parameter. A call on an
object nobody can tell is not one of them, and the log says how many
there were. Highlights are read or written for a variable.

-- lib/dgdtools.yml --
root: .
driver_config: mud.dgd
-- lib/mud.dgd --
include_dirs = ({ "/include" });
-- lib/include/std.h --
#define BASE "/std/base"
-- lib/std/base.c --
int weight;
int query_weight() { return weight; }
void set_weight(int w) { weight = w; }
-- lib/obj/a.c --
#include <std.h>
inherit BASE;

void create() {
    int n;
    n = query_weight();
    set_weight(n + 1);
    weight++;
    ob->query_weight();
}
-- lib/obj/b.c --
inherit "/std/base";
int heavy() { return query_weight() > 10; }
-- script --
initialize lib
open lib/obj/a.c
# Once it is linted, the log has said what project it is of.
diagnostics lib/obj/a.c

# A function, with and without its declaration; and from the
# declaration, in a file that is not open.
references lib/obj/a.c 5:10
references lib/obj/a.c 5:10 decl
received window/logMessage

# A global variable of an inherited object.
references lib/obj/a.c 7:5 decl

# An object: the inherit statements of it, however they write its path.
references lib/obj/a.c 1:2

# A macro, from its #define: an inherit statement that is about the
# object names the macro too.
open lib/include/std.h
references lib/include/std.h 0:10 decl

# A local, in its function only.
references lib/obj/a.c 4:9 decl

# Nothing: a call on an unknown receiver, a keyword.
references lib/obj/a.c 8:10
references lib/obj/a.c 3:1

# Highlights: a local written and read, a global incremented, a
# function.
highlight lib/obj/a.c 5:4
highlight lib/obj/a.c 7:5
highlight lib/obj/a.c 6:6
highlight lib/obj/a.c 3:1
